title: “Sí al desarme, sí a la paz” Closes in Nuevo Laredo: 83 Firearms Destroyed
excerpt: Nuevo Laredo's voluntary gun-exchange campaign closed with 83 firearms and 2,748 cartridges destroyed, and 273,000 pesos paid in incentives to residents who turned weapons in.
content:
Nuevo Laredo's voluntary gun-exchange campaign, “Sí al desarme, sí a la paz,” closed with 83 firearms of various calibers and 2,748 cartridges destroyed, and 273,000 pesos paid in incentives to residents who turned weapons in, according to a local news roundup from Prensa Unida.

The campaign was run by the Mexican military, SEDENA, together with the municipal government. It operated November 18, 19, 23, and 24 at the Monumento a Los Fundadores, where military personnel staffed a module to receive weapons from residents, according to CML Noticias' report on the campaign's launch.

Residents could voluntarily surrender firearms in exchange for a cash incentive, with no questions asked and no investigation, according to the launch coverage. Military personnel evaluated each weapon under the program's official schedule to set the payment, then destroyed the weapon once the exchange was accepted.

At the launch, officials said the goal was to prevent accidents in homes and help build safer surroundings for families. A rifle turned in on the first day was destroyed in front of the media, and the person who surrendered it received a little more than 13,000 pesos, according to Sin Censura.

The campaign was part of a broader push for a culture of prevention and peace in Nuevo Laredo, with the military and the municipal government urging residents to turn in firearms, cartridges, and other weapons kept at home.

Sources: Prensa Unida / Mas Noticias NLD, November 25, 2026; CML Noticias, November 17, 2026; Sin Censura, November 17, 2026.
